rows.27:e948:
You see it?
It's just an ordinary clock, nothing special about it.
It's pretty dusty, though.
Let's open it up.{p}
rows.27:e9d0:
...There's no battery in it anymore.
That's why it doesn't run.
But you know, this clock is strange.
Say you move the hands, right?
Before you know it, they've gone back to 10:20.{p}
rows.27:ebec:
"Whoa!"
The other five all screamed at once.
They looked, and on the wall where the clock had hung, there was a stain like a human face.
For an instant, it looked like a skull.
...But when they looked closely, it was just a stain.{p}
rows.27:ece4:
"A skull-shaped stain★"
{f:I|I} hurriedly cut in.
A stain that looked like a skull{f:, he said|...}?
Wasn't that the same thing I'd seen in the restroom earlier{f:|}?
Was he telling me that same stain was behind that clock{f:|}?
Somehow, I had a bad feeling about this.
Unable to put it into words, I said nothing, and Hosoda gave {f:me|me} a puzzled look.
And then the story went on.{p}
rows.27:ee44:
...Why not?
I just know you and I would get along great.
Come on, be my friend.{p}You will, won't you? Please?
rows.27:eeb4: I don't want to be your friend
rows.27:eec4: Oh well, I'll be your friend
rows.27:eeec:
That's cruel.
Do you really enjoy hurting me that much?
Were you always such a mean person?
Hosoda looked at {f:me|me} reproachfully.
...Oh well, I guess there's no helping it{f:|}.
{f:I|I} nodded.
"{f:Sorry|I'm sorry}. {f:Fine, I'll be your friend|Let's be friends}."{p}
rows.27:f000:
Okay, got it.
Then I'll tell you.
After all, it's a request from you, my friend.
...The three of them headed off together to the faculty room.
You go straight down the hallway, turn the corner, and the faculty room is right there.
It's not a long way at all.
They still looked fairly relaxed.
But when they turned the corner, there was no faculty room.
In front of them, the very hallway they should have just walked down stretched on and on.
When they looked back, there was the classroom door.
They hadn't moved a single step.
But how could that be?
Just to be sure, they started walking again.
They walked to the end of the hallway and turned the corner.
...Sure enough, a long hallway stretched on in front of them.{p}
rows.27:f248:
And behind them, the classroom door.
That settled it.
They were trapped.
Who had trapped them, they didn't know.
How, they didn't know either.
All they knew was that space had twisted around into something like a Mobius strip.
You know, that loop you make from a ribbon with one twist in it, where if you trace it with your finger, you can't tell the back from the front anymore.
"I can't take this anymore☆"
The girl who'd burst into tears earlier screamed.
But this time, the other girl didn't comfort her.
I guess she was in no state to.
She was shaking like a leaf.
As the only guy left, he must have felt it was all on him.{p}{a}{f:, what would you do|, what would you do in his place}?
rows.27:f538:
First, naturally, they checked the windows.
It had been a muggy day, so the windows were left open to let in even a little breeze.
But at some point, they'd been closed.
Without a word, the three of them tried to open them.
Because once you start wondering who closed them... you just keep imagining scarier and scarier things.
But the windows wouldn't open.
It was like they'd rusted shut.
Ridiculous, right?
Those windows had been open just a moment ago.
After a few tries, someone must have hit their limit.
"I'm going home! I'm going home, I said☆"
The one shrieking wasn't the girl who'd been crying, but the one who'd been comforting her.{p}
rows.27:f748:
She grabbed her bag and ran out of the classroom.
"Hey, wait!"
He started to go after her, but then the other girl would be left all alone, and he couldn't do that to her.
He stayed put.
And that turned out to be the right choice.
Because a few seconds later...{p}
rows.27:f8bc:
The two of them went over to the door and saw something crawling in the hallway, where the lights had gone out.
What was it?
As they strained their eyes, it inched a little closer.
It was the girl who had run off.
Still lying face down, she was desperately lifting her head and reaching out her hand.{p}
rows.27:f9d4:
"Help... me..."
A hoarse voice begged for help.{p}
rows.27:faa0: And then something big was flung down at the two of them, landing at their feet.{p}
rows.27:faf8: They jumped out of the way, and saw that it was an arm, still tightly clutching a school bag.{p}
rows.27:fb50:
"Eeeeeeeek☆"
The girl screamed.
At the sound, the darkness in the hallway swelled.
The darkness itself was alive.{p}
rows.27:fc74:
The endless darkness spreading outside the windows.
And that darkness surging straight toward them.
The window glass was creaking.
Any second now, the windows would break.
And once that happened, there would be no way left for them to survive.
...In that case.
An idea came to him.{p}What do you think it was?
rows.27:fd90: Sacrifice the girl and escape himself
rows.27:fdb4: Sacrifice himself and let the girl escape
rows.27:fdf0:
He opened the door to the hallway.
The darkness was only a few meters away now.
He swallowed hard and shoved the girl standing next to him.
She had trusted him completely, so she stumbled out into the hallway without a struggle.
The darkness caught her by the legs.
She was dragged to the floor, and she looked up at him.
With eyes full of resentment, as if she couldn't believe it.{p}
rows.27:10040:
As he ran, he spotted an emergency exit.
He was saved!{p}
rows.27:10080:
He took a run at the door and slammed into it.
The door shook, but it wouldn't open.{p}
rows.27:100d4:
But there was no time left to try anywhere else.
The darkness could catch up with him at any moment, after all.{p}
rows.27:10144:
He threw his body against the door again and again.
And at last, the door opened.{p}
rows.27:101a0:
As he burst through, stumbling, someone caught him.
Relieved that he'd finally reached somewhere safe, he nearly sank to the ground.
But whoever had caught him kept pulling at him, trying to make him stand up.
"No, no, you mustn't rest in a place like this.
You're going this way..."
A voice he knew.{p}
rows.27:102bc:
He looked up with a start. It was that girl.
The girl he'd shoved out and fed to the darkness.
Between her lashes there were no whites and no pupils, only spreading darkness.
He tried to run, but she held him tight and wouldn't let go.
The corners of her mouth curled into a small smile.
"Let's go... together..."
He froze, and the next instant, the darkness wrapped around him.{p}
rows.27:10400:
"...And that's how it went.
The next day, the teachers searched for the six of them.
But not a single one was ever found.
As if they'd melted away."
Hosoda finished his story.
It seemed to have gotten a little darker than before{f:|}.{p}
rows.27:104e0:
{f:I|I} found myself looking around.
I didn't want to stay here much longer{f:|}.
"Thank you very much.
Well then, shall we head back to the club room?"
As {f:I|I} tried to wrap things up, Hosoda cut me off.{p}
rows.27:105dc:
"Hold on.
The story isn't over yet.
Why do you think I went to the trouble of coming all the way here?"
"How would I know?
It's late, so maybe we should call it a day..."
"The darkness here, you see, is still alive."
Hosoda whispered, out of nowhere.
"It's alive, and it still wants food... Look."
He pointed at a corner of the classroom.{p}
rows.27:10724:
Maybe it was my imagination, but the darkness seemed to squirm on the old floorboards.
My mouth went dry in an instant.
No way... it had to be my imagination{f:|, right}.
I only thought I saw something{f:|}.{p}
rows.27:107e8:
...Hosoda was smiling from ear to ear.
"You don't want to believe it, huh?
I can't blame you, but think about how I'd know a story like this."
Clowning around, he rolled both his eyes.{p}
rows.27:10894:
Then his eyeballs bulged out.
More than halfway out of their lids.
Looking closely, they weren't real eyeballs.
They were cloudy, round, opaque glass... just like marbles.{p}
rows.27:10948:
With a hard clack, clack, the two marbles dropped to the floor and rolled away.
And from behind them, an infinite darkness peered out, stretching on forever.
"It's very spacious inside the darkness.
If I don't bring in more of our kind, I get so lonely I can't stand it..."
Hosoda, with eyes of darkness, came closer.
Would {f:I|I}, too, stare into the darkness and wander around like this, looking for more of my kind{f:|}...?
As the darkness swallowed me from my hands and feet inward, {f:I|I} kept dazedly thinking about that.{p}
rows.27:10af8:
He turned to face the girl.
"I'm going to clear us a path somehow.
While I do, you get away."
"But what about you?"
"Once you're out, I'll be right behind you."
That's what he said, but he didn't really believe he'd get away too.
I guess he thought, if only the girl could make it...
{f:If it were me|I'm sure}, {f:I could never think like that|those two were good friends, just like us}.
He opened the door to the hallway.{p}
rows.27:10cb0: The darkness was only a few meters away now.{p}
rows.27:10cf4: He swallowed hard and flung his own bag out there.{p}
rows.27:10d3c:
With a squelching crunch, the darkness swallowed the bag.
Just how many victims were inside that pitch-black belly?
He shuddered in spite of himself.
But he couldn't stand there like that forever.{p}
rows.27:10e04:
He shoved the girl away.
She stumbled off in the direction away from the darkness.
"Run, hurry!"
Shouting that, he raised a chair over his head.
And he hurled himself at the darkness.{p}
rows.27:10eb0:
The darkness spread wide for an instant and engulfed him.
For a moment, he lost consciousness.
...Maybe it was really a lot longer than that, though.
But when he came to, it didn't feel like that much time had passed.
Yeah, that's right.
The darkness didn't eat him.{p}
rows.27:11058:
And then, what do you know, a monster came running at him from over there.
An ugly body thickly covered in purple scales, and huge, bulging eyes.
Drool was streaming from its mouth, which was split all the way to its ears, and it was screaming words he couldn't make out.
He felt his life was in danger.
Looking around, he saw a bat lying on the ground that the baseball team must have forgotten to put away.{p}
rows.27:11188: He picked it up and went at the monster, swinging.{p}
rows.27:111c8: Head, shoulders, arms, he didn't care where, he just beat it.{p}
rows.27:11298:
At the same moment, someone grabbed him from behind and pinned his arms.
It was the janitor, with a rigid look.
"What are you doing?!"
What did it look like he was doing?
He'd been taking out this monster.
He was about to say so, and he looked down at the monster's corpse.{p}
rows.27:1139c:
But the one lying there was the girl he was supposed to have saved from the darkness. Blood was running from her head, and she lay limp with her eyes shut.
One look told him she wasn't alive anymore.{p}
rows.27:11448:
"I heard a racket and came to see, and here you are beating this girl!
Why on earth would you do this to her★"
The janitor asked him.
There was no way he could answer, right?
What he'd been beating was supposed to be a monster.
But it wasn't, was it?
Which leaves only one possibility.
In his eyes, his friend, the girl, had looked like a monster.
So when she ran over to him because she was worried, he thought she was attacking him.
Instead of eating him, the darkness warped his sight, I think.
Knowing full well what it would lead to.{p}
rows.27:11648:
If so, that's unbelievably cruel, isn't it?
Because his misfortune didn't end there.
What do I mean?
The next day, the teachers searched the building.
And... they found the bodies of the other four, one after another.
The darkness got all of them, I guess.
Apparently they were in a horrible state.
And that got pinned on him too.
Nobody listened to his side of the story.
After all, he'd been caught red-handed.{p}
rows.27:117d4:
What happened to him after that?
...Well, I don't know.
I'd guess he got locked up somewhere, like a prison or a juvenile detention center.
The story was over.
{f:I|I} raised my lowered head and looked at Hosoda.{p}
rows.27:118b4:
...The one sitting there wasn't Hosoda.
No, it wasn't even human.
Six eyes, like compound eyes, peered out through patchy tufts of hair.
Its crooked, jagged teeth glinted.{p}
rows.27:1194c:
"A... a monster★"
{f:I|I} jumped back.
The monster was saying something as it came toward me.
Wasn't there anything{f:|}?
A weapon, anything I could fight it with.
I felt around in my pockets, and my fingertips touched something hard.
A box cutter{f:|}.
The one I'd used for the club, when we were clipping articles for a scrapbook.
{f:I|I} held it ready.
The monster's arm reached for the box cutter.
I won't let you!
{f:|Frantically, }I swung the cutter, and the blade slashed the monster's eye!{p}
rows.27:11b1c:
Spurting green blood, the monster slowly collapsed.
Breathing hard, {f:I|I} looked around.
I felt like I'd been with someone until just a moment ago.
...Had I?
{f:I|I} {f:had been alone from the start, hadn't I|feel like I was alone from the start}?
{f:That's right|Yes, that's it}.
{f:I|I} {f:am|am} all alone.
I defeated the monster, so the ruler of this world is {f:me|me}.
...Still, I'm tired{f:|}.
{f:I|I} yawned and curled up next to the monster's corpse.
I'll sleep a little.
After all, there's nothing left to threaten {f:me|me}.{p}
rows.27:11d44: Just then, I thought I heard the darkness that had crept up to my feet let out a laugh.{p}
rows.27:11d90:
Right, they searched the hallway too.
If they could find the spot where space was warped, they might be able to escape through it.
With their eyes peeled wide, they went along feeling over the walls and floor.
"Oh, look!"
One of the girls pointed at a corner of the hallway.{p}
rows.27:11f1c:
When they peered through, they could see a green plain on the other side!
They tried scratching around the crack.
Bits crumbled away.
The wall fell apart almost absurdly easily.{p}
rows.27:11fd4:
And spread out before them was, sure enough, a vast plain.
"We're saved!"
Shouting that, the girls ran out onto the grass.
Then they turned back to him.
"Hurry up, come on!"
But he couldn't take that step.
He'd realized something was wrong.
A grassland stretching as far as the eye could see didn't seem like it could be in Japan, for one thing.{p}
rows.27:12118:
While he hesitated, the wall started to grow.
The part that had crumbled swelled back up all on its own.
Before his eyes, the hole in the wall shrank to about half its size.
He tried scratching at it, but the wall that had been so fragile a moment ago was now as hard as a steel plate.
"Hurry, come over here!"
The girls started to panic.
But all the while, the hole kept closing.{p}
rows.27:1225c:
And finally, it was back to being just the crack it had started as.
He'd been left behind alone, on this side of the world.
In warped space, no less.
But in the end, the girls stayed missing too.
They'd made it out, but maybe the other side of the crack was warped space as well.{p}
rows.27:12384:
What did he do after that, you ask?
He's still missing.
And so is everyone else, while we're at it.
Maybe they're all still in here somewhere.{p}
rows.27:12408:
...Just kidding.
Hosoda finished his story.
{f:I|I} couldn't help speaking up.
"Going out of your way to tell a story like that here, of all places.
That's in bad taste."{p}
rows.27:12604:
When I looked back, an identical long hallway stretched on behind me.
What was going on{f:|}?
Had Hosoda's story come true{f:|}?
But in the story, the classroom door was supposed to be behind them{f:|}.
And yet...
{f:I|I} hurriedly ran back the way I'd come.
No matter how far I ran, the classroom door didn't appear.
This can't be!
When I looked a moment ago, the hallway was only about ten meters long.
Had {f:I|I}, too, wandered into the warped space{f:|}?
I didn't want to admit it.
{f:I|I} kept running.
Maybe someday I'd find the door.
So I ran.
Ran.
Ran.
Ran.
Then I noticed that at some point, a shadow had started running alongside {f:me|me}.
I turned to look.{p}
rows.27:128a4:
A half-skeletonized man was running with his teeth bared.
His eyes turned to {f:me|me}.
{f:I|I} knew who he was.
He was the guy from the story just now{f:|}.
He'd kept on running for all those long years, even after dying and turning to bone{f:|}.
His eyes looked somehow happy.
It was only natural, now that he had {f:me|me} as a companion{f:|, I suppose}.{p}He and {f:I|I} would probably keep running forever down that endless hallway.
Through the warped world.{p}
rows.27:12a3c:
Right.
He decided to start looking with the nearest restroom.{p}
